name: Bengaluru
tagline: India's garden city and easy-living tech capital.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Sep, Oct, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: Cool, clear November to February is best, framed by the Republic Day flower show. Skip the June-to-September monsoon showers.

ourTake.lede: Bengaluru is a city to eat, drink and browse rather than to sightsee; treat it as a comfortable base with excellent weather and use it as the launch point for Coorg, Hampi or a Nandi Hills morning. The old cantonment and the Lalbagh gardens are the genuine pleasures; the traffic is the genuine hazard, so cluster your plans by neighbourhood. Don't over-schedule monuments here.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a mild-weather city break with strong food, craft bars and easy weekend escapes into the hills.
ourTake.skipIf: You are after monuments or beaches; this is a garden city built for living, not sightseeing.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: The Oberoi, Bengaluru
credentials: The Oberoi Group, recognised luxury house
Houses Wabi Sabi, Condé Nast Traveller India Top Restaurant Awards 2024 (No. 20)
items.description: A serene Oberoi in the heart of the city, rooms opening onto rain-tree gardens and a pool, a green pause off MG Road.

items.name: Taj West End, Bengaluru
credentials: Taj Hotels, recognised heritage house
Established 1887, Bengaluru's oldest hotel
items.description: The city's oldest hotel, from 1887, twenty acres of heritage gardens, colonial gables and centuries-old rain trees.

items.name: The Leela Palace Bengaluru
credentials: MICHELIN Guide, listed hotel
The Leela Palaces, Hotels & Resorts, recognised luxury house
items.description: A grand modern palace on the airport road, copper domes, a lotus lagoon and one of the city's most opulent lobbies.

items.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Bangalore
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide, Bengaluru (recognised)
Marriott, The Ritz-Carlton
items.description: India's first Ritz-Carlton, among the largest rooms in the city, a rooftop pool and a seven-strong dining-and-bar floor.

items.name: ITC Windsor, a Luxury Collection Hotel
credentials: Marriott, Luxury Collection
LEED, world's first Zero Carbon hotel; LEED Platinum-rated
Houses Dakshin, long-running Times Food Guide 'Best South Indian Restaurant'
items.description: A colonial-Bengaluru grande dame, and the first hotel in the world to earn LEED Zero Carbon certification.

items.name: ITC Gardenia, a Luxury Collection Hotel
items.area: Central Business District (Residency Road, near Cubbon Park)
credentials: Marriott, Luxury Collection
LEED, Asia's first Platinum hotel; LEED Zero Carbon & LEED Zero Water
items.description: A vertical garden rising above Cubbon Park, Asia's first LEED Platinum hotel, and a benchmark for responsible luxury.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel Bengaluru at Embassy ONE
credentials: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts, recognised luxury house
Houses Copitas, The World's 50 Best Discovery; Asia's 50 Best Bars (No. 38, 2023)
items.description: Sleek, contemporary Four Seasons service in a twin-tower address, home to Copitas, one of the city's most awarded bars.

items.name: Conrad Bengaluru
items.area: Central Business District (Kensington Road, near Ulsoor Lake)
credentials: Hilton, Conrad Hotels & Resorts
Forbes Travel Guide, Bengaluru (recognised)
items.description: A bright, contemporary Hilton-Conrad above Ulsoor Lake, generous rooms, a lively rooftop and easy city-centre access.

items.name: JW Marriott Bengaluru Prestige Golfshire Resort & Spa
credentials: Marriott, JW Marriott
Forbes Travel Guide, Bengaluru (recognised)
items.description: A resort-scale JW beside a lake and golf course near the airport, space, spa and countryside calm outside the city.

items.name: Shangri-La Bengaluru
items.area: Central Business District (Palace Road, near Cubbon Park)
credentials: Shangri-La Group, recognised luxury house
Recognised leading city hotel, large-format luxury and banqueting
items.description: One of the city's largest luxury hotels, big rooms, a serious pool and Shangri-La's assured pan-Asian service.

items.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
credentials: Republic Day and Independence Day flower shows are the two set-pieces of the year
items.description: The garden Hyder Ali laid out and Tipu Sultan filled with plants from Persia, Kabul and France, 240 acres of lawns, a Mughal spine and the 1889 Glass House modelled on London's Crystal Palace, which still hosts the biannual flower show. Come at dawn, before the walkers thin out, for the birdsong and the cool.

items.name: The Lalbagh Rock & Kempegowda Tower
credentials: A Geological Survey of India National Geological Monument
items.description: A vast open dome of peninsular gneiss inside the garden, dated by the Geological Survey of India to some 3,000 million years, among the oldest exposed rock on earth. One of the four watchtowers Kempegowda raised to mark the city's old boundary sits on top; the climb takes five unhurried minutes and the view opens over the whole garden.

items.name: Cubbon Park
items.description: The green lung at the heart of the old city, nearly 300 acres of bamboo, rain trees and shaded avenues, laid out in 1870. Sunday mornings the roads close to cars and it belongs to walkers, cyclists and readers. A discreet, easy hour between heavier sights.

items.name: State Central Library (Seshadri Iyer Memorial Hall)
items.description: The unmistakable brick-red neoclassical hall standing in the green of Cubbon Park, built in 1915 to honour a Dewan of Mysore. Behind the columns sits Karnataka's central library, which holds a copy of nearly every book published in the state. The exterior and the rose gardens in front are the draw.

items.name: Attara Kacheri (Karnataka High Court)
items.description: A two-storey stone building of intense red, Corinthian columns and Gothic lines from 1864, facing the Vidhana Soudha across the road. It still houses the High Court, so the interior is off-limits, but the facade, one of Colonel Sankey's set of red landmarks around Cubbon Park, is worth the pause.

items.name: Vidhana Soudha
items.description: The seat of Karnataka's legislature and the city's grandest building, a monumental Neo-Dravidian pile in Bangalore granite, finished in 1956, its domes and pillars floodlit on Sunday and holiday evenings. The interior is not open to casual visitors; this is a photograph-from-the-lawns and after-dark sight.

items.name: Bangalore Palace
items.description: The Wadiyar family's Tudor-revival residence of turrets, battlements and carved-wood interiors, begun in 1878 and inspired by Windsor. Still privately owned by the royal family, it opens as a museum, the ballroom, the hunting trophies and Art-Deco arches make an unhurried couple of hours. A private guide earns their fee here.

items.name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
items.description: A two-storey pavilion built entirely of teak, all carved pillars, cusped arches and floral fresco, finished in 1791 as Tipu's summer retreat inside the old fort. Small, quiet and unusually intact, the kind of place a good guide brings alive with the story of the man who called it 'the envy of heaven'.

items.name: Bangalore Fort & Delhi Gate
items.description: What survives of the mud fort Kempegowda raised and Hyder Ali rebuilt in stone, the Delhi Gate, a stretch of rampart and a small Ganesha temple, where the British breach of 1791 is still marked. A short, atmospheric stop paired naturally with Tipu's palace next door.

items.name: Dodda Basavana Gudi (Bull Temple)
items.description: One of the largest Nandi shrines anywhere, a single granite bull some 15 feet tall, dark and butter-smoothed, carved under Kempegowda in the 16th century. The Kadalekai Parishe groundnut fair each Kartika month floods the lanes around it. A living, unpolished temple, not a monument behind ropes.

items.name: Bugle Rock Park
items.description: A sheer outcrop of ancient rock beside the Bull Temple, named for the bugle once sounded from its top to warn the town. One of Kempegowda's watchtowers still stands here, and the gardens below are a shaded, local kind of quiet. Easily walked together with the temple.

items.name: Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple
items.description: A rare rock-cut cave shrine to Shiva, attributed to Kempegowda in the 16th century, with monolithic stone discs and trishuls in its forecourt. Its marvel is engineering: on Makar Sankranti in mid-January the setting sun's rays pass between Nandi's horns to light the lingam for a few minutes, a feat of deliberate alignment.

items.name: Halasuru Someshwara Temple
items.description: The oldest temple in the city, a Shiva shrine whose sanctum is traced to Chola work of around a thousand years ago, expanded under Vijayanagara with an ornate pillared hall and gateway tower. Little visited by tourists, richly carved, and a window onto Bengaluru long before the Garden City.

items.name: ISKCON Sri Radha Krishna Temple
items.description: One of the largest ISKCON temples in the world, opened in 1997 on a seven-acre hillock, a soaring glass-and-gold complex with a cow shelter, prasadam halls and long evening aartis. Immaculate, calm and easy to fold into a morning; pure-vegetarian throughout, as Karnataka tends to be.

items.name: St Mary's Basilica
credentials: The first church in Karnataka to be elevated to a minor basilica
items.description: Among the city's oldest churches and the first in Karnataka raised to minor basilica, a graceful Gothic hall of pointed arches, Corinthian columns and stained glass, elevated by Pope Paul VI in 1973. Its September feast draws half a million; on an ordinary day it is cool and unhurried.

items.name: HAL Aerospace Museum & Heritage Centre
credentials: India's first aerospace museum
items.description: India's first aerospace museum, opened in 2001 on the Hindustan Aeronautics campus, decades of aircraft and helicopters, engine cutaways, a mock control tower and a flight simulator. A genuine treat for a multi-generational visit, and a nod to the aviation industry that helped make this a tech city.

items.name: Visvesvaraya Industrial & Technological Museum
items.description: The hands-on science museum named for the engineer-statesman Sir M. Visvesvaraya, packed with working exhibits on engines, electronics, space and biotechnology. Beside Cubbon Park and built for curious children, the reliable answer to a rainy afternoon with the family.

items.name: National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA Bengaluru)
items.description: The southern outpost of the national modern-art collection, set in the restored Manikyavelu Mansion with a garden of old trees. Works by Tagore, Amrita Sher-Gil, Raja Ravi Varma and the moderns hang in cool, well-lit rooms, a serene, uncrowded hour of Indian art.

items.name: Government Museum
credentials: Among the oldest museums in India (established 1876)
items.description: One of the oldest museums in India, opened in 1876 in a red neoclassical building near Cubbon Park. Vijayanagara and Halebidu sculpture, ancient coins and stone inscriptions thousands of years old sit inside; the architecture matches the High Court and library nearby. Modest in scale, deep in age.

items.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Planetarium
items.description: A well-run planetarium with a Sky Theatre, science park and centre, opened in 1989 and popular with families for its dome shows. An easy, air-conditioned interlude that pairs neatly with an evening near the palace or Cubbon Park.

items.name: Ulsoor Lake (Halasuru Lake)
items.description: One of the city's oldest and largest lakes, its origins in Kempegowda's time, dotted with little islands and ringed by a walking path. Row, pedal or motor across it in the cool of the evening, an easy, central pause rather than a destination in itself.

items.name: Commercial Street
items.description: One of the oldest and most crowded shopping streets in the city, clothes, footwear, gold and fabric spilling from small shops, threaded with old eateries. Loud, tactile and best walked with a driver waiting; the heart of Bengaluru's bargaining tradition.

items.name: MG Road & Brigade Road
items.description: The old spine of modern Bengaluru, the tree-shaded MG Road promenade and the bustle of Brigade Road, lined with bookshops, silk houses, brands and cafes. The city's cosmopolitan face, and the natural place to feel its unhurried, English-speaking ease.

items.name: Church Street
items.description: A short, cobbled street that is the city's most walkable stretch of cafes, bookshops, bars and small restaurants. Long the haunt of Bengaluru's readers and diners, pedestrianised at weekends, and the easiest way to taste the pub-and-cafe culture on foot.

items.name: Chickpet
items.description: A four-century-old wholesale bazaar, the traditional home of the silk and sari trade, narrow lanes stacked with textiles that dressmakers across the city still swear by. Chaotic and authentic; go with a guide who knows which shop for what.

items.name: UB City
items.description: The city's luxury address, a tower complex of international boutiques, jewellers and fine-dining rooftops around a marble concourse. When you want the polished, air-conditioned end of Bengaluru retail rather than the street bazaars, this is it.

items.name: Cauvery Emporium
items.description: The Karnataka government's flagship handicrafts emporium, fixed-price, government-authorised, and the safe place to buy sandalwood carving, Channapatna lacquer toys, rosewood and silk without haggling or doubt over quality. The sensible first stop for gifts to carry home.

items.name: KSIC / Mysore Silk showroom
credentials: Mysore silk was Karnataka's first GI-tagged product; genuine pieces carry a hologram and unique code
items.description: The Karnataka Silk Industries counters where you buy the genuine article, Mysore silk, woven from pure mulberry with real gold zari, carrying its own GI protection and hologram. Demand runs so high that fresh stock is released only on set days; a private advisor can smooth the visit.

items.name: The microbrewery & dining scene
credentials: Widely regarded as the birthplace of India's craft-beer movement
items.description: Bengaluru is India's craft-beer capital, brewpubs opened here before anywhere else in the country, and the city now runs on garden restaurants, rooftop bars and a genuinely serious food scene. Karnataka vegetarian cooking is a highlight in its own right; a good concierge can line up the tables that matter.

items.name: Bannerghatta Biological Park
items.description: A large zoo and safari park about an hour out, a jeep safari past free-ranging lions, tigers and bears, plus a butterfly park and rescue centre. A reliable half-day with children, and the closest brush with wildlife you can have inside the city's limits.

items.name: Dodda Alada Mara (Big Banyan Tree)
items.description: A single banyan roughly four centuries old that has spread its aerial roots across some three acres, one of the largest trees in India, so wide it reads as a small forest. A short, quiet drive out of the city and a genuinely arresting natural sight.

items.name: Nrityagram
items.description: A dance village built in mud and stone, founded in 1990 to keep Odissi and other classical forms alive as a living gurukula. Visits are structured and best arranged in advance, a serene, cultured half-day quite unlike anything else near the city.

items.name: Nandi Hills sunrise
items.description: The classic pre-dawn drive out of Bengaluru, up to a 1,400-metre hilltop where a sea of cloud lies below the sunrise, with Tipu's fort, a Shiva temple and the sheer cliff of Tipu's Drop at the summit. Leave the city very early; the light before six is the whole point.

items.name: Skandagiri dawn trek
items.description: A hill fort at around 1,450 metres, climbed in the dark to reach the summit for a cloud-sea sunrise. More effort than Nandi and quieter for it, for the traveller who wants the walk as much as the view. Best with a guide and a permit sorted in advance.

items.name: Ramanagara (the Sholay rocks)
items.description: The dramatic granite hills where the film Sholay was shot, now a draw for rock-climbers and, at Ramadevarabetta, a vulture sanctuary. An easy detour on the road to Mysore for anyone drawn to raw rock and cinema history.

items.name: Mysore, Amba Vilas Palace
items.description: The Wadiyars' Indo-Saracenic palace and one of India's grandest royal residences, domes, stained glass, carved doors and a durbar hall of astonishing colour. On Sunday nights and during Dasara it is lit by close to a hundred thousand bulbs. The centrepiece of the great day-trip from Bengaluru.

items.name: Mysore, Chamundi Hill & the Nandi
items.description: The hill above Mysore crowned by the Chamundeshwari temple, with the whole city laid out below. On the way down stands a monolithic Nandi carved from a single rock, a quick, photogenic stop. Best paired with the palace on a full Mysore day.

items.name: Brindavan Gardens
items.description: The terraced pleasure gardens below the Krishnaraja Sagar dam, symmetrical parterres, fountains and a musical-fountain show at dusk. Timeless, a touch old-fashioned, and a fine evening close to a Mysore day if you stay the night nearby.

items.name: Srirangapatna
items.description: Tipu Sultan's island capital on the Cauvery, the ancient Ranganathaswamy temple, the fresco-covered Daria Daulat Bagh summer palace, the Gumbaz where Tipu and his parents lie, and the fort walls where he fell in 1799. Dense with history, and an easy add-on to the Mysore road.

items.name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
items.description: Riverine islets on the Cauvery that Karnataka's most important bird sanctuary, storks, egrets, cormorants and basking marsh crocodiles, seen from a small boat. A gentle, birding-forward stop that pairs with Srirangapatna on the way to or from Mysore.

items.name: Shivanasamudra Falls
items.description: The Cauvery splitting into the twin cascades of Gaganachukki and Barachukki, thundering in the monsoon and after, beside one of Asia's earliest hydroelectric stations, built in 1902. Loveliest from July to about October; a scenic day out southeast of the city.

items.name: Coorg (Kodagu) coffee country
items.description: The misty coffee hills the British called the Scotland of India, plantation estates, waterfalls, spice and the distinct Kodava culture. Too far for a comfortable day trip, but the natural one- or two-night escape from Bengaluru, and a heritage-estate stay is the way to do it.

items.name: Devanahalli Fort
items.description: A well-preserved 16th-century oval fort with rounded bastions and old temples inside, and the birthplace of Tipu Sultan, marked within the walls. Quiet, uncommercial and barely ten minutes off the airport road, so it slots into an arrival or departure day.

items.name: Taj West End (the grounds)
items.description: A colonial-era hotel set in twenty acres of heritage garden, rain trees, orchids and low tiled bungalows that go back to 1887. Even for a garden lunch or high tea rather than a stay, it is the gentlest way to feel the old Garden City the name once promised.

items.name: Sankey Tank
items.description: A calm colonial-era tank built by Colonel Sankey in 1882, ringed by a leafy walking path in one of the city's oldest, most gracious neighbourhoods. A short, restful stop in Malleswaram, best combined with a wander through the old market lanes nearby.

items.name: Malleswaram & the 8th Cross market
items.description: One of Bengaluru's oldest quarters, still steeped in old-city character, the 8th Cross flower-and-produce market, filter-coffee rooms, silver and silk shops and Sampige Road's temples. A walk here, ideally with a guide, is the city's living, un-touristed heart.

items.name: Vishveshwarapura (VV Puram) food street
items.description: An evening lane given over entirely to Karnataka street food, obbattu, dosas, holige, sweets and sugarcane juice served from open stalls. Pure-vegetarian, boisterous and genuinely local; the tastiest hour in the old south of the city, best on foot after dark.

items.name: Farmlore
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 2025, No. 68
American Express One To Watch Award 2025 (Asia's 50 Best Restaurants)
items.description: An eighteen-seat farm-to-table table on a working farm outside the city, India's most talked-about new fine-dining experience.

items.name: Naru Noodle Bar
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 17
items.description: A tiny, chef-led ramen counter that feels lifted from a Tokyo backstreet, and sells out in seconds.

items.name: Wabi Sabi
items.area: Central Business District (The Oberoi, MG Road)
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 20
items.description: The Oberoi's polished Japanese-Nikkei room, sushi, sashimi and Peru-inflected plates in a hushed, grown-up setting.

items.name: NĀVU
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 27
items.description: A chef-led tasting-menu restaurant whose name means 'us' in Kannada, Karnataka roots reimagined with pan-Asian ideas.

items.name: Lupa
items.area: Central Business District (Church Street / MG Road)
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 31
items.description: Manu Chandra's Tuscan-villa dining room, seasonal European cooking and one of the city's best-looking rooms.

items.name: Bengaluru Oota Company
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 32
items.description: A tiny tasting-room celebrating Gowda and Mangalorean home cooking, 'Karnataka on a plate', by reservation only.

items.name: Karavalli
items.area: Central Business District (Vivanta Bengaluru, Residency Road)
credentials: The World's 50 Best Discovery
Condé Nast Traveller India Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 39
items.description: Since 1990, the definitive South-West-coast kitchen, called 'the most famous South Indian restaurant in the world'.

items.name: Dakshin
items.area: Diplomatic / leafy Bengaluru (ITC Windsor, Sankey Road)
credentials: Times Food Guide, repeated 'Best South Indian Restaurant'
The World's 50 Best Discovery, ITC Hotels signature dining
items.description: Regal South Indian dining since the 1980s, the four southern states on one grand, silver-service menu.

items.name: Copitas
credentials: The World's 50 Best Discovery
Asia's 50 Best Bars (No. 38, 2023)
items.description: The Four Seasons rooftop that eats as well as it drinks, small, precise plates alongside one of India's most awarded bars.

items.name: Bar Spirit Forward
items.area: Central Business District (Lavelle Road, Hotel Southern Star)
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025, No. 37
Condé Nast Traveller India Top Restaurant Awards 2024, No. 40
items.description: A bar-led kitchen where the food is built around the drinks, seasonal, pan-Indian small plates that keep pace with the glasses.

items.name: The Permit Room
credentials: The Bombay Canteen / Bombay Sweet Shop group, recognised hospitality house
Condé Nast Traveller India, recognised bar-restaurant
items.description: A retro South-Indian bar-diner in cheerful lime and cane, filter-coffee cocktails and dosa-batter nostalgia, done with real polish.

items.name: Soka
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025, No. 28 (highest-ranked bar in Bengaluru)
items.description: An intimate, art-filled cocktail room where local flavours meet Art Deco, Bengaluru's highest-ranked bar in Asia.

items.name: ZLB 23
items.area: Old Airport Road (The Leela Palace Bengaluru)
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025, No. 31 (up from No. 40 in 2024)
items.description: A hidden Prohibition-era speakeasy behind the Leela's chocolate room, velvet, chandeliers and jazz, climbing the Asia list yearly.

items.name: Bar Spirit Forward
items.area: Central Business District (Lavelle Road, Hotel Southern Star)
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025, No. 37
items.description: A drinks-first bar built on seasonality, yams and local produce turned into both cocktails and small plates.

items.name: Copitas
credentials: The World's 50 Best Discovery
Asia's 50 Best Bars (No. 38, 2023)
items.description: The Four Seasons' rooftop bar, city-light views, minimalist craft cocktails and the calm precision of the house.

items.name: Toit Brewpub
credentials: Recognised pioneering craft microbrewery, Bengaluru's flagship brewpub
Regularly named among India's best breweries
items.description: The brewpub that defined Bengaluru's craft-beer era, three floors, house lagers and the city's most reliably buzzing room.

plan.heading: 2 days in Bengaluru, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Check into The Oberoi on MG Road, its rooms set among old rain trees.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lalbagh Botanical Garden and its glasshouse, then the colonial avenues of the cantonment.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Karavalli at the Taj, the long-standing coastal Konkan and Malabar kitchen.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Bangalore Palace and the Tipu Sultan Summer Palace, then a filter-coffee stop in Basavanagudi.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Contemporary art at the National Gallery of Modern Art, and silk and sandalwood at the state emporia.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dine at Naru Noodle Bar or Farmlore, the tasting-menu farmhouse on the city's edge, before departure.

items.name: MG Road / Cubbon Park area
items.description: Central cantonment heart near the park and clubs; best for easy access and green calm.

items.name: Indiranagar
items.description: The dining and nightlife district; suits those who want restaurants and bars within walking distance.

items.name: Ulsoor / Halasuru
items.description: Older, quieter and lake-side; for travellers who prefer a residential, local feel.

events.name: Karaga
events.note: An ancient, atmospheric night procession through the old city, one of Bengaluru's oldest living traditions.

events.name: Dasara (nearby Mysuru)
events.note: The royal Mysuru festival is an easy trip away and among South India's grandest, with the illuminated palace.

events.name: Bengaluru literature and arts festivals
events.note: A strong cool-season calendar of lit-fests and cultural events across the city.

events.name: Deepavali
events.note: The southern Diwali, celebrated warmly with lamps and sweets across the city's homes and temples.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay around UB City or the leafy central district for the best hotels and restaurants; the climate is mild year-round, the one Indian metro that needs no acclimatising.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Arrive at Kempegowda International Airport (BLR), a polished terminal about an hour north of the city; a chauffeured car handles the transfer.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car with driver is best given the sprawl and traffic; the airport is far, so build the drive into your timing.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Strong 5G and business-grade wifi everywhere; an Indian eSIM or Jio/Airtel SIM is effortless.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The Indian rupee (INR); cards and UPI dominate, cash is rarely needed, and tipping around ten percent is customary.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Mild almost year-round thanks to elevation; Oct-Feb is the loveliest, cool and clear. Avoid Apr-May, the warmest and driest stretch before the rains, and expect afternoon showers through Jun-Sep.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Home hub: Kempegowda International (BLR) is a primary origin, so no connection needed from Bengaluru and a 2-2.5 hour hop from Delhi or Mumbai on Vistara or IndiGo. The airport is modern but roughly 40km from the centre; use the 080 Lounge and pre-book a chauffeur, as the drive into town can take well over an hour in traffic.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: Routine vaccines plus Hepatitis A and typhoid advised; use sealed or filtered water. Bengaluru is safe and relaxed by big-city standards; the main friction is traffic and long transfer times rather than any safety concern.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Exceptionally easy; the city is deeply vegetarian and Jain options are common. South Indian vegetarian is a highlight, from the institution that is MTR to the refined thalis and dosas across town.
